brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 7.4% profit vs peers' 5.0%, and the market shows modest headroom below ₹0.85/pc at volume.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging, targeting the ₹0.65–0.80/pc band the market allows at higher volume.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc for the 28 mm induction-wad PP cap (currently market-typical at ₹0.85–0.95/pc)
priceAsk.basis: The market ask shows 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec'. They keep 7.4% profit vs similar firms' 5.0% — that 2.4 percentage-point cushion means room in their price. With our volume and a tighter spec or longer commitment, the lower band is justified.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (15 Days After Receipt instead of 30) in exchange for a price cut of about 3.5%.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier costs us ₹1.64 L in cash. They borrow money at about 7.02%, so 15 days early is worth roughly 3.5% annualised to them — trade that for a matching price cut.

brief.financialLeverage: PGP Glass is healthy and profitable: CARE A+ / Stable rating, ₹3373.51 Cr revenue, keeping 7.4% profit (peers keep 5.0%). Their cash is tied up for 78 days vs peers' 71 days, and they pay suppliers in 29 days vs peers' 42 — so cash moves a bit faster out than in, making early payment appealing. But we're tiny — 0.01% of their sales (₹39.99 L) — so we have almost no volume pull on our own. The play is to bundle a longer-term commitment or threaten to qualify a second source (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) to get attention, then trade faster payment for the price cut their margin can absorb.

evidence.point: They keep 7.4% profit, well above the 5.0% peers keep — cushion for a price cut
Market research shows the 28 mm PP cap typically sells at ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue), makes pharma bottles/caps/preforms — the top second-source candidate, health B (65/100).

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr), strong and profitable (health B 73/100) — robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (market backup)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): pan-India manufacturer, medium confidence — potential resin or component source at maker pricing.

risks: We're tiny (0.01% of their sales) — on our own we have almost no pull. Bundle more SKUs, commit for 2–3 years, or line up Manjushree/Mold-Tek and show we're serious about a second source.
They have EPF payment delays and pending legal cases flagged — watch for any supply hiccups or distractions that could delay our orders.
Distress signal shows Altman Z-score 1.45 (grey zone) — not in trouble today, but not rock-solid either. Don't squeeze so hard that cash dries up and quality or delivery slips.

The market headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc assumes 'higher volume / looser spec'. If we can't commit more volume or relax a spec, the achievable cut may be smaller — clarify what 'higher volume' means in the room.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a three-year deal and pay you 15 days faster — in return, we need your price to come down to the ₹0.65–0.80 band the market supports at volume, because we're also qualifying Manjushree as a second source.
